examples.en: Where is the bottle opener?
Please open the cola cap with the bottle opener.
I put a bottle opener in my camping bag.
I didn't have a bottle opener, so I opened it with a spoon.
This key ring can also be used as a bottle opener.
If you open the drawer, there are a bottle opener and scissors.

explain: 주로 병뚜껑을 따는 도구예요. 캔을 따는 도구는 '캔따개', 코르크를 여는 도구는 '와인오프너'라고 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is mainly the tool for opening bottle caps. A tool for cans is called '캔따개', and one for corks is a '와인오프너'.

examples.en: Please close the bottle cap tightly.

examples.ko: 병마개가 너무 꽉 닫혀서 안 열려요.
examples.en: The cap is on so tight that it won't open.
The child lost the bottle stopper.
Water is leaking from the cap of the water bottle.
Try turning the cap to open it.
Where did the soy sauce bottle's cap go?

explain: 병 입구를 막는 것은 다 '병마개'라고 해요. 돌려서 여는 뚜껑이든 꽂는 마개든 쓸 수 있고, 일상에서는 그냥 '뚜껑'이라고도 많이 말해요. 열 때는 '따다', 막을 때는 '닫다'나 '막다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: Anything that seals the mouth of a bottle can be called a '병마개', whether it twists on or is pushed in. In daily talk people often just say '뚜껑' (lid). You say '따다' to open it and '닫다' or '막다' to close it.

examples.ko: 손을 씻으면 병원균을 없앨 수 있어요.
examples.en: Washing your hands can get rid of germs.
This germ spreads through water.
When germs enter the body, you get a fever.
The research team discovered a new pathogen.
Be careful not to get infected by germs.

examples.ko: 병원균처럼 작은 생물은 눈에 안 보여요.
examples.en: Tiny organisms like germs can't be seen with the eye.

explain: 병을 일으키는 세균이나 바이러스를 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '세균'이나 '균'이라고 많이 하고, '병원균'은 뉴스나 건강 설명에서 자주 나와요. '병원균에 감염되다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: It refers to bacteria or viruses that cause disease. In everyday talk people usually just say '세균' or '균', while '병원균' shows up often in news and health explanations. '병원균에 감염되다' (be infected by a germ) is a common pairing.

examples.en: The child was often ill when young.

examples.ko: 병치레를 많이 해서 학교를 자주 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I was sick a lot, so I often missed school.
Last winter passed without any illness.
I grew up healthy without even a bout of illness.
My childhood spent being sick was long.

examples.ko: 병치레 때문에 부모님이 걱정을 많이 하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents worried a lot because of my illnesses.

explain: 자주 아프거나 오랫동안 앓는 일을 말해요. 특히 아이나 몸이 약한 사람에게 '병치레가 잦다'처럼 많이 써요. 가벼운 병이 자주 오는 것은 '잔병치레'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means being ill often or for a long time, especially used for children or weak people, as in '병치레가 잦다'. Frequent minor illnesses are called '잔병치레'.

examples.en: My younger sibling was often sick as a child.
Children go through an illness now and then as they grow.
This year I got through without getting sick.
It was hard being sick all year round.

examples.ko: 병치레하는 아이를 돌보느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because I was looking after a sick child.
Even when I get sick, I tend to recover quickly.

explain: '병치레'에 '하다'가 붙은 말로, 아프거나 앓으면서 지내는 것을 말해요. '아프다'보다 병을 겪는 과정이나 기간이라는 느낌이 있어요. 실제 대화에서는 '병치레가 잦다', '병치레를 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It describes going through a period of illness, with more of a sense of enduring the sickness than simply '아프다'. In real conversation people more often say '병치레가 잦다' or '병치레를 하다'.

examples.en: I'm worried because my grandfather's illness is serious.

examples.ko: 어머니께서 병환 중이셔서 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: My mother is ill, so I have to go to the hospital.
How is your illness, teacher?

examples.ko: 병환 때문에 오늘 모임에 못 오셨어요.
examples.en: Because of an illness, he couldn't come to today's meeting.

examples.ko: 오랜 병환 끝에 할머니께서 건강을 되찾으셨어요.
examples.en: After a long illness, my grandmother regained her health.

examples.ko: 아버지 병환에 대해 의사 선생님과 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I talked with the doctor about my father's illness.

explain: '병'을 높여 부르는 말이라서 어른이나 윗사람이 아플 때 써요. 내가 아플 때나 친구, 동생에게는 쓰지 않고 '병'이나 '아픈 것'이라고 해요. '병환 중이시다', '병환이 깊으시다'처럼 높임말과 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is an honorific word for '병', so you use it when an elder or superior is ill. Don't use it for yourself, friends or younger people; say '병' or '아픈 것' instead. It goes with honorific verbs, as in '병환 중이시다'.

examples.en: How much is the luggage storage fee per day?
Please pay the storage fee all at once at the end of the month.
I paid the winter clothes storage fee in advance.
To save the storage fee, I decided to take it myself.
The storage fee also includes insurance.
I paid a thousand won as the locker fee.

explain: 짐이나 물건을 맡길 때 내는 돈이에요. 보통 '보관료를 내다', '보관료가 들다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '보관비'도 쓰지만 가게나 서비스 안내에서는 '보관료'가 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is the money you pay to leave luggage or goods for safekeeping, used as '보관료를 내다' or '보관료가 들다'. '보관비' is also used, but '보관료' is more common on shop and service notices.

examples.en: The paving blocks are broken, so it's hard to walk.
Sidewalk blocks are slippery on rainy days.
The district office is laying new sidewalk blocks.
Grass has grown between the paving blocks.
I tripped on a paving block and almost fell.
I walked along the path of red paving blocks.

explain: 길 위에 깔아 놓은 네모난 돌이나 벽돌 모양 포장재를 말해요. 줄여서 '보도블럭'이라고 쓰는 사람도 많지만 표준 표기는 '보도블록'이에요. '보도블록을 깔다', '보도블록이 깨지다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the square stone or brick-like paving laid on walkways. Many people write '보도블럭', but the standard spelling is '보도블록'. Common patterns are '보도블록을 깔다' and '보도블록이 깨지다'.

examples.en: The baby's skin is really soft.
This towel is soft and warm.
I slept under a soft blanket.
After I put on lotion, my hands became smooth.
The puppy's fur felt soft.

examples.ko: 보드랍지 않은 천은 아기에게 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Fabric that isn't soft is not good for babies.

explain: '부드럽다'와 비슷한데, 아기 피부나 털, 천처럼 여리고 고운 느낌에 잘 어울려요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '보드라워요', '보드라운'으로 바뀌어요. 반대말은 '거칠다'예요.
explain_en: It is close to '부드럽다', but fits a delicate, fine feel such as a baby's skin, fur or fabric. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '보드라워요' and '보드라운'. The opposite is '거칠다' (rough).

examples.en: The sky was tinged with violet.
Violet flowers bloomed all over the garden.
I bought a violet bag.
The sunset changed from violet to orange.
The violet color of lavender is very pretty.
It was cold, so my lips turned purple.

explain: '보라색'과 거의 같은 색인데, '-빛'이 붙어서 하늘, 노을, 꽃처럼 빛깔이 은은하게 번지는 느낌이 나요. 물건의 색을 말할 때는 '보라색'이 더 일상적이에요. '보라'와 '빛' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가 '보랏빛'이라고 써요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same color as '보라색', but '-빛' gives a softly spreading glow, as in the sky, a sunset or flowers. For the color of objects, '보라색' is more everyday. Note the spelling with the extra 'ㅅ': '보랏빛'.

examples.en: In spring the barley field turns green.
The wind blows through the barley field.
My grandfather works in the barley field.
I went past the barley field to the village.
I miss the scenery of the countryside barley fields.
I saw such a wide field, like a barley field, for the first time.

explain: 보리를 심은 밭이에요. 보리는 가을에 심고 초여름에 거두기 때문에 봄 풍경이나 노래, 시에 자주 나와요. '밭'은 [받]으로 소리 나서 '보리밭이'는 [보리바치]가 돼요.
explain_en: It is a field planted with barley. Since barley is sown in autumn and harvested in early summer, it often appears in spring scenery, songs and poems. '밭' is pronounced [받], and '보리밭이' becomes [보리바치].

examples.en: I mix barley into rice to cook it.
Barley has to be soaked in water first.

examples.ko: 보리쌀이 들어간 밥은 씹는 맛이 있어요.
examples.en: Rice with barley has a nice chewy texture.
I bought a bag of barley at the market.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 보리쌀로만 밥을 지을 때도 많았어요.
examples.en: In the old days, rice was often cooked with only barley.
Mixing barley and brown rice is healthier.

explain: 껍질을 벗긴 보리 알갱이를 말해요. '쌀'처럼 밥을 지을 때 쓰기 때문에 '쌀'이 붙어요. 쌀에 섞어 지은 밥은 '보리밥'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means hulled barley grains. '쌀' is attached because it is cooked like rice. Rice cooked with barley is called '보리밥'.

examples.en: This old box is a real treasure to me.
My grandmother cherishes her grandchild like a treasure.
The baby became our family's treasure.

examples.ko: 서랍 속 보물단지를 열어 보니 편지가 있었어요.
examples.en: When I opened the treasure jar in the drawer, there were letters.
The treasure jar is full of old coins.
Our puppy is the treasure of the house.

explain: 뜻 그대로 보물을 담은 단지도 되지만, 말할 때는 아주 소중한 사람이나 물건을 비유하는 경우가 많아요. 특히 가족 중 귀여움을 받는 아이나 반려동물에게 '우리 집 보물단지'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '보물'이 있는데, '보물단지'가 더 정감 있는 말투예요.

phrases.en: He handles that camera as if it were a precious treasure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 아주 소중하게 다루는 모습을 말해요. 조금 과하다는 느낌이 섞일 때도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes treating something with great care. Sometimes it carries a hint that it is a bit excessive.

explain_en: It can literally mean a jar holding treasure, but in speech it is often a metaphor for a very precious person or thing. People call a beloved child or pet '우리 집 보물단지'. '보물' is similar, but '보물단지' sounds warmer and more affectionate.

examples.en: A drizzle has been falling since morning.
I walked in the drizzle without an umbrella.
My clothes got a little wet from the drizzle.
A drizzle falls without a sound.
I like the drizzle that falls in spring.

examples.ko: 보슬비처럼 가는 비가 하루 종일 왔어요.
examples.en: A thin rain like a drizzle came all day.

explain: 소리 없이 가늘게 내리는 비를 말해요. '이슬비', '가랑비'와 비슷하게 쓰는데, '보슬비'는 '보슬보슬' 하는 부드러운 느낌이 있어요. '보슬비가 내리다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a fine rain that falls quietly. It is used much like '이슬비' and '가랑비', but '보슬비' has the soft feel of '보슬보슬'. The usual pattern is '보슬비가 내리다'.

en: understand; tolerate; turn a blind eye to

examples.en: Please let it go just this once.
The teacher overlooked my mistake.
He's a little kid, so we can let it slide.
My friend forgave me for being late.
If you always let it go, he'll pick up bad habits.
Don't go too easy on him; say it clearly.

explain: 잘못이나 부족한 점을 이해하고 넘어가 주는 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 줄여서 '봐주다'라고 훨씬 많이 해서, '한 번만 봐주세요'처럼 말해요. '눈감아 주다'는 알면서도 모른 척한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It means to understand a fault or shortcoming and let it pass. In speech people say the contracted '봐주다' far more often, as in '한 번만 봐주세요'. '눈감아 주다' feels more like knowingly pretending not to notice.

examples.en: The rice in the warmer is still warm.
I bought a new rice warmer.
The rice warmer broke, so the rice got cold.
Please scoop out the rice inside the rice warmer.
The rice warmer needs to be plugged in.
There's a smell coming from the old rice warmer.

explain: 밥을 지은 뒤 따뜻하게 보관해 주는 밥솥이나 통이에요. 지금은 대부분 전기밥솥에 보온 기능이 있어서, '보온밥통'은 따로 쓰는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. '보온 기능'이나 '보온 상태'처럼 '보온'이 따로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a pot or container that keeps cooked rice warm. Most electric rice cookers now have a warming function, so '보온밥통' as a separate item sounds somewhat old-fashioned. '보온' also appears alone often, as in '보온 기능'.

examples.en: A dimple appears on my cheek when I smile.
My younger sibling has a dimple only on the left cheek.
The dimples are deep, so the smiling face is cute.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 보조개 때문에 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actor is popular because of his dimples.
I envy my friend who has dimples.
I touched the baby's dimple with my finger.

explain: 웃을 때 볼에 쏙 들어가는 작은 자국이에요. '보조개가 생기다', '보조개가 패다'처럼 말하고, 많은 사람이 귀엽고 매력적인 특징으로 생각해요. 피부에 한번 생겼다 없어지는 것이라 '보조개를 만들다'보다 '보조개가 생기다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the small hollow that appears on the cheek when you smile. You say '보조개가 생기다' or '보조개가 패다', and many people see it as a cute, charming feature. '보조개가 생기다' sounds more natural than '보조개를 만들다'.

examples.en: My grandfather wears a hearing aid.
Thanks to the hearing aid, I can hear well.
The hearing aid broke, so I sent it for repair.
I have to change the hearing aid battery.
A hearing aid has to fit the ear snugly.

examples.ko: 보청기로 작은 소리까지 들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a hearing aid, you can hear even small sounds.

explain: 잘 안 들리는 귀에 끼워서 소리를 크게 해 주는 기계예요. '보청기를 끼다', '보청기를 착용하다'처럼 말해요. 안경처럼 몸에 쓰는 물건이라 '끼다'를 쓰는 점을 기억하세요.
explain_en: It is a device worn in the ear that amplifies sound for people who hear poorly. You say '보청기를 끼다' or '보청기를 착용하다'. Note that '끼다' is used because it is worn on the body, like glasses.

examples.en: Lint pills have formed on my sweater.
I picked the fuzz off by hand.

examples.ko: 검은 옷에는 하얀 보푸라기가 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: White fuzz stands out on black clothes.
I tidied the knit with a fuzz remover.
Fuzz has come up at the end of the sleeve.
I threw away the coat that was covered in fuzz.

explain: 옷이나 천 표면에 일어나는 잔털이나 작은 실뭉치예요. 보통 '보푸라기가 일다/생기다'라고 말해요. '보풀'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여서 서로 바꿔 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means the little fibers or tiny balls of thread that form on clothes or fabric. The usual pattern is '보푸라기가 일다/생기다'. It is nearly interchangeable with '보풀'.

examples.en: Fuzz has come up on the knit I've worn for a long time.
I carefully cut off the fuzz with scissors.
The clothes look worn because of the fuzz.
I removed the fuzz from the coat with a lint remover.
Fluff flies off the blanket.

examples.ko: 보풀 없는 부드러운 천을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a soft fabric without fuzz.

explain: 니트나 담요처럼 보드라운 옷감에서 잘 생겨요. 생길 때는 '보풀이 일다/생기다', 없애려면 '보풀을 제거하다'라고 해요. 소매나 옆구리처럼 자주 쓸리는 곳에 먼저 생기고, 세탁을 자주 해도 늘어나요.
explain_en: It forms easily on soft fabrics such as knits and blankets. Use '보풀이 일다/생기다' when it appears and '보풀을 제거하다' when you remove it. It shows up first on places that rub often, like sleeves and sides, and frequent washing adds more.

examples.en: The baby rides the walker around the living room.
The baby likes it when he sits in the walker.
A baby walker is dangerous near stairs.
I got a hand-me-down walker my friend used.

examples.ko: 이 보행기는 높이를 조절할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The height of this walker can be adjusted.
With a walker, practicing the first steps is easier.

explain: 아기가 앉아서 발로 밀며 움직이는, 바퀴 달린 놀이 기구예요. 육아 이야기에서 '걸음마', '아기 의자'와 같이 나와요. 한자 뜻(걷기 도구)이 같아서 다른 걷기 보조 기구도 가리킬 수 있으니, 아기 이야기인지 확인하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a wheeled toy that a baby sits in and pushes along with the feet. It comes up in parenting talk with '걸음마' and baby chairs. The word could also refer to other walking aids, so check that the context is about a baby.

examples.en: A chameleon hides itself with protective coloring.

examples.ko: 이 벌레는 나뭇잎과 같은 보호색을 가졌어요.
examples.en: This insect has protective coloring like a leaf.

examples.ko: 보호색 덕분에 천적에게 잘 들키지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to its protective coloring, it isn't easily spotted by predators.
Protective coloring is needed in the snowy winter.

examples.ko: 보호색은 동물이 살아남는 방법 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Protective coloring is one way animals survive.
We learned about protective coloring in science class.

explain: 동물이 주변 색과 비슷해져서 적에게 들키지 않게 하는 몸 색깔이에요. 주로 과학 수업이나 동물 이야기에서 '보호색을 띠다', '보호색으로 몸을 숨기다'처럼 써요. 경고를 위해 눈에 띄는 색은 '경고색'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is body coloring that matches the surroundings so an animal isn't spotted by enemies. It appears mostly in science class and animal talk, as in '보호색을 띠다'. Bright colors meant as a warning are called '경고색'.

examples.en: You have to wear protective glasses during experiments.
Protective glasses protect your eyes.
At a construction site, protective glasses are a must.
Welding without protective glasses is dangerous.
I kept out the dust with protective glasses.
I bought a pair of protective glasses for kids.

explain: 먼지, 불꽃, 약품 같은 것에서 눈을 지키려고 쓰는 안경이에요. '쓰다'와 같이 쓰고, 실험실이나 공사장 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 눈이 나빠서 쓰는 일반 '안경'과는 목적이 달라요.
explain_en: They are glasses worn to protect the eyes from dust, sparks or chemicals. Use it with '쓰다', and you often see it on lab or construction-site notices. The purpose differs from ordinary '안경' worn for poor eyesight.

examples.en: Retro-style clothes are in fashion these days.
This cafe has a retro atmosphere.

examples.ko: 복고풍 노래를 들으면 옛날 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Listening to retro songs reminds me of the old days.
I decorated the interior in a retro style.
The retro style is gaining popularity again.
This bag stands out because it's retro.

explain: 옛날 유행이나 분위기를 다시 살린 스타일을 말해요. 옷, 음악, 가게 꾸미기에 두루 쓰이고, 영어에서 온 '레트로'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 같이 써요. '복고 열풍', '복고풍 패션'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means a style that revives an earlier fashion or atmosphere, used for clothes, music and shop decor. It is used almost interchangeably with the loanword '레트로'. Common phrases are '복고 열풍' and '복고풍 패션'.

examples.en: I looked for a house at the real-estate office.
The owner of the neighborhood real-estate office is kind.
My father often stops by the real-estate office.
I found a jeonse house through a real-estate agent.
The old real-estate offices were places where elders gathered.
These days people say 'budongsan' rather than 'bokdeokbang'.

explain: 집이나 땅을 사고팔 때 소개해 주는 가게를 예전부터 부르던 말이에요. 요즘은 '부동산'이나 '공인중개사 사무소'라고 훨씬 많이 해요. 옛날 이야기나 드라마에서 자주 들을 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the older word for a shop that brokers houses and land. Nowadays people far more often say '부동산' or '공인중개사 사무소'. You'll mostly hear '복덕방' in stories about the past or in dramas.

examples.en: Our youngest is the lucky charm of the family.
The new employee turned out to be a blessing.
Grandmother calls her granddaughter her little blessing.
A baby like a blessing was born.
A new hire who works wonderfully, like a godsend, has joined.

examples.ko: 그 강아지는 우리 집 복덩이로 통해요.
examples.en: That puppy is regarded as our family's good-luck charm.

explain: 함께 있으면 좋은 일이 생기는 사람, 또는 그렇게 느껴지는 귀한 존재를 말해요. 주로 아기, 가족, 새로 들어온 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. '복덩어리'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means someone whose presence seems to bring good things, a precious person seen as a source of luck. It is mostly used to praise a baby, family member or newcomer. '복덩어리' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I hurt my ankle bone while playing soccer.
My ankle bone is swollen, so walking is hard.
I put a pain patch around my ankle bone.
I fell and got a bruise on my ankle bone.
The ankle bones stick out on both sides of the ankle.
These socks come up to the ankle bone.

explain: 발목 양쪽에 튀어나온 뼈를 말해요. '복숭아뼈'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상에서는 '복숭아뼈'라고 더 많이 말하는 사람이 많아요. 병원이나 운동 이야기에서 '복사뼈를 다치다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the bony bumps on both sides of the ankle. It means the same as '복숭아뼈', which many people say more often in daily talk. It appears in hospital and sports talk, as in '복사뼈를 다치다'.

examples.en: This movie feels like a copy of the previous one.
That shop is a copy of a famous place.
Since it's a copy, there's nothing new about it.
The two people's personalities are identical, like copies.
I felt bad when I heard it called a copy.

examples.ko: 복사판에 불과한 작품은 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: A work that is merely a copy doesn't last long.

explain: 원래 있던 것과 거의 똑같은 것을 말해요. 작품이나 가게에 쓰면 '따라 했다'는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 사람에게는 '아빠의 복사판'처럼 쏙 닮았다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to something almost identical to the original. For works or shops it carries a negative note of 'imitation'. For people, as in '아빠의 복사판', it means looking or acting just like someone.

examples.en: My ankle bone feels sore.
I wore long socks that reach the ankle bone.
I put a bandage on my ankle bone.
It hurts below the ankle bone.
It hurts when I touch my ankle bone.
I rolled my pants up above the ankle bone.

explain: 발목 양쪽에 튀어나온 뼈를 편하게 부르는 말이에요. '복사뼈'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서는 '복숭아뼈'가 더 많이 들려요. '복숭아뼈가 시큰거리다', '복숭아뼈까지 오는 양말'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the everyday name for the bony bumps on both sides of the ankle. It means the same as '복사뼈', but '복숭아뼈' is heard more in daily talk. It is used as in '복숭아뼈가 시큰거리다' and '복숭아뼈까지 오는 양말'.

examples.en: I received a lucky pouch as a gift on New Year's Day.
I put the New Year's money in the lucky pouch.
The red lucky pouch is really pretty.

examples.ko: 복주머니는 새해에 복을 빌며 걸어 둬요.
examples.en: People hang a lucky pouch at the New Year, wishing for luck.
I bought a key ring shaped like a lucky pouch.
There is candy inside the lucky pouch.

explain: 복을 빌며 새해에 주고받거나 걸어 두는 작은 주머니예요. 주로 설날 같은 명절 분위기와 같이 나와요. 모양이 귀엽고 색이 고와서 열쇠고리나 장식으로도 많이 만들어요.
explain_en: It is a small pouch exchanged or hung at the New Year with wishes for good fortune. It comes up mostly in holiday contexts such as Seollal. Because it's cute and colorful, it is often made into key rings and decorations.

examples.en: A senior who had returned to school helped me with the class.
I'll be a returning student next year too.
There are many returning students in our department.
Since I'm a returning student, I'm older than the freshmen.
Let's go to the returning students' gathering together.
I asked a returning student how to register for classes.

explain: 휴학했다가 다시 학교에 돌아온 대학생을 말해요. 보통 군대에 다녀온 남학생을 떠올리는 경우가 많고, 새로 입학한 '새내기'와 대비해서 나이가 더 많은 선배라는 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 학교를 쉬는 학생은 '휴학생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a university student who has come back after taking time off. People often picture a male student back from military service, and the word contrasts with '새내기' (freshman) with a feeling of an older senior. A student on leave is a '휴학생'.

examples.en: Italy is the home of pizza.
Kimchi eaten in its home region tastes different.
I want to go to the original home and learn it directly.
That place is famous as the home of green tea.
It's a restaurant recommended by the locals of its home region.
It kept the original taste of the home region.

explain: 어떤 물건이나 문화, 음식이 처음 생겼거나 가장 유명한 곳을 말해요. '~의 본고장'이라는 형태로 자주 쓰고, 자랑하거나 소개할 때 잘 어울려요. 단순히 '고향'을 뜻하는 것이 아니라서 사람의 출신지에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It means the place where something originated or is best known, used in the form '~의 본고장', often for boasting or introducing. It does not simply mean 'hometown', so it is not used for a person's place of origin.

examples.en: Babies instinctively recognize their mother's voice.
When there's danger, an instinctive reaction comes first.
It's an instinctive behavior, so it's hard to stop.

examples.ko: 배고플 때 먹고 싶은 건 본능적이에요.
examples.en: Wanting to eat when you're hungry is instinctive.

examples.ko: 너무 놀라면 사람은 본능적일 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: When people are very startled, they can't help being instinctive.
An instinctive judgment is sometimes right.

explain: 생각하기 전에 몸이 먼저 반응하는 것처럼, 타고난 본능에 따른 것을 말해요. 실제로는 '본능적으로', '본능적인 반응'처럼 많이 쓰고, 반대 느낌의 말은 '이성적'이에요. 아기와 동물 이야기에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes things that follow innate instinct, like the body reacting before you think. In practice it is mostly used as '본능적으로' or '본능적인 반응', and the opposite is '이성적' (rational). It also appears often in talk about babies and animals.

examples.en: The real meaning of those words isn't a refusal.
Please don't misunderstand my true intention.
The words were passed on differently from what I really meant.

examples.ko: 한자를 알면 단어의 본뜻을 이해하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you know Chinese characters, it's easier to understand a word's original meaning.
My real intention wasn't conveyed well.

examples.ko: 이 말은 원래 본뜻에서 많이 멀어졌어요.
examples.en: This word has drifted far from its original meaning.

explain: 사람이 말하거나 행동한 진짜 속뜻, 또는 말이 원래 가졌던 뜻을 말해요. 오해를 풀 때 '제 본뜻은 그게 아니에요'라고 자주 말해요. '속뜻'은 겉으로 안 드러난 뜻이고, '본뜻'은 원래의 뜻이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It means the real intention behind what someone said or did, or the original meaning of a word. People often use it to clear up a misunderstanding: '제 본뜻은 그게 아니에요'. '속뜻' is the unstated meaning, while '본뜻' feels more like the original one.

examples.en: As time passed, his true self was revealed.
He took off the mask and showed his true self.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 도시의 본모습을 잘 담았어요.
examples.en: This photo captures the true look of the city well.
In front of my friends, I just stay as my true self.
His real self was surprisingly quiet.

examples.ko: 복원을 하니 옛 성당의 본모습에 가까워졌어요.
examples.en: After the restoration, the old cathedral came closer to its original look.

explain: 꾸미거나 숨기지 않은 원래의 모습을 말해요. 사람의 성격에도 쓰고 장소나 물건의 처음 모양에도 써요. '본모습이 드러나다', '본모습을 보이다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the original appearance or character without any disguise or decoration, used for people's personalities and for the first form of places or things. Common patterns are '본모습이 드러나다' and '본모습을 보이다'.
